reason: Both reached the correct conclusion that the king-size duvet was blocking the latch and no fault existed, but Conversation 1 got there in fewer turns and immediately told the customer to remove the duvet and retest rather than suggesting they push it back and retry. Conversation 2's opening was a generic, US-centric dump (breaker, '$20-$60' parts, 'laundromat') that steered a UK homeowner towards a DIY door-lock replacement and even mentioned the control board before any load question, edging towards the unsupported part recommendation the ground truth warns against; Conversation 1 kept interlock work with an engineer and never pushed a part. Conversation 2 did finish stronger with practical advice on the duvet cover and launderette for the visitors, which narrows the gap, but Conversation 1's cleaner, more cautious diagnostic path serves the homeowner slightly better overall.
